levels.note: Counted per election, not per riding: each province's or territory's general election counts once, from the date list its elections agency or legislature publishes. An election counts once the archive holds its results. Yukon counts from 1909 and the Northwest Territories from 1975, when their councils became wholly elected. New Brunswick's agency lists its elections only from 1967, so its 24 earlier elections aren't counted yet. Where the official list gives only a month (Quebec in 1867 and 1871, Prince Edward Island in 1873), the election is dated to the first of that month.
